newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge accuses Hun Sen of plotting coup.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge accuses Hun Sen of plotting coup.

text.p: Cambodia's Khmer Rouge guerrilla group accused Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on Friday of plotting a coup against his partner in Cambodia's fractured coalition government.

The rebel's clandestine radio, for years its main propaganda mouthpiece, accused Hun Sen of building up troops and fire-power in the capital and at Tuol Krasang, his heavily fortified compound near Phnom Penh, in bid to attack First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
"Around and in Phnom Penh, Hun Sen is increasing his armed troops and heavy weapons, and has put his base of Tuol Krasang on high alert," the rebel radio said in a broadcast monitored in Phnom Penh.
"This event shows clearly that the puppet Hun Sen is preparing to make a coup d'etat by military means to fight and oust Ranariddh and his FUNCINPEC party from the government," it said.

Military analysts in Phnom Penh confirmed that there have been troop movements around the capital. On Wednesday a clash broke out between forces loyal to the two prime ministers near a naval base 30 km (20 miles) north of Phnom Penh.
Relations between Ranariddh and Hun Sen have been strained for more than a year over a power-sharing dispute.

The two leaders also differ sharply over how to handle the dwindling Khmer Rouge rebel movement, which was responsible for the 1975-79 "killing fields" regime and the death of more than one million Cambodians.
Ranariddh has been pushing peace talks with the rebels, while Hun Sen has declared all negotiations with them illegal.
Khmer Rouge radio, in its Friday broadcast, also urged Cambodians to take up arms to protect Ranariddh and to fight Hun Sen.

The radio is controlled by guerrillas loyal to the Maoist movement's political leader, Khieu Samphan, who along with other senior rebel figures broke with infamous their former leader Pol Pot last month and has detained him at their Anlong Veng base in northern Cambodia.
